practice.prompt: An adjective only takes an ending when it stands...
choices: before a noun (attributive): der alte Mann
at the start of a sentence

practice.prompt: "Der Mann ist alt." — the adjective "alt" here takes...
Nominative masculine after "der": "Der alt___ Mann wohnt hier."
Accusative masculine after "den" — the trap: "Ich kenne den alt___ Mann."
Nominative feminine after "die": "Die jung___ Frau liest."
Dative feminine after "der": "Ich helfe der jung___ Frau."
Nom/Akk neuter after "das": "Das klein___ Kind schläft."
Plural after "die" — always -en: "Die neu___ Autos sind teuer."
The short rule for adjectives after der/die/das:
choices: -e in 5 slots (nom. der/die/das + acc. die/das), -en everywhere else
-er in the singular, -e in the plural
exactly the same weak endings as der/die/das
